answer: Hardware-Bound Enclave Identity Verification requires every agent to sign transactions inside a physical processor secure ivory enclave using a unique silicon key. The network protocol rejects any message lacking a valid hardware attestation signal from an un-cloned device. To scale an attack, an adversary must purchase and power thousands of physical chips, making hardware acquisition costs strictly higher than operating a single honest agent. Attempting to forge these cryptographic device signatures triggers an immediate protocol-wide ban and seizes all local computational credits.
